What Is A Temperature Blanket? Every day I knit one row based on the temperature outside.
Each color tells a story:
| Temperature (°F) | Color |
|—————–|——-|
| 100°F+ | ⬛ Black |
| 90–100°F | 🟪 Pink |
| 80–90°F | 🟥 Red |
| 70–80°F | 🟧 Orange |
| 60–70°F | 🟨 Yellow |
| 50–60°F | 🟩 Green |
| 40–50°F | 🔵 Light Blue |
| 30–40°F | 🔵 Dark Blue |
| 20–30°F | 🟣 Purple |
| 10–20°F | ⬜ Gray |
| Month Start | ⬜ White |
2026 So Far *📸 Photo of blanket progress here*
What The Colors Are Telling Me Your reflection on what the pattern reveals about this year’s
weather and climate here!
Why I Do This As a climate scientist I spend my days working with temperature
data in spreadsheets and satellite imagery. The temperature blanket
is my way of making that data tangible — something I can hold,
something that grows with the year, something that tells the story
of climate in a way that a graph never quite can.
Every unusual color is a conversation starter. Every long stretch
of red is a reminder of why this work matters.

👋 Hi, I’m Mira! Ecosystems are disappearing faster than we can map them… and the services they provide to people are disappearing with them.
As a PhD Candidate in the Department of Earth and Environment at Boston University, my goal is to comprehend what we have before we lose it. I am a biogeographer interested in understanding how anthropogenic climate change and urbanization affect ecosystem distribution and their associated services. Using a combination of satellite remote sensing, data science, and ground-truth validation, I established an annual ecosystem map of Belize spanning 2015–2026 with 85% accuracy. My current research investigates how landscape dynamics, such as adjacency, proximity, and fragmentation, affect the services these ecosystems provide to people locally and globally. Ultimately, my work is about understanding what we stand to lose, and giving communities and conservationists the tools to act before it is too late.
My PhD is supported by the NSF-Strong Coasts Grant, reflecting the broader coastal resilience context of my work in Belize.
🎓 Education Ph.D. Earth and Environment — Boston University (expected May 2027) M.A. Earth and Environment — Boston University, 2022 B.A. Environmental Studies — Mount Holyoke College, 2017 Head Class Agent 🌿 Fieldwork In February 2026, my team from Boston University joined forces with Wild Earth Allies to ground-truth ecosystems around Placencia, Belize. We travelled by boat through riparian forests, hiked submontane forests, and confirmed a dozen distinct forest types with some of the best botanists and ecologists in the region.
📸 Read the full story and see photos →

I have partnered with the New England Aquarium as a whale watch naturalist since 2015. Stellwagen Bank National Marine Sanctuary is world reknowned as a feeding ground for humpback whales. See recent sightings and photos by my colleagues: @whalesofstellwagen
I am also an avid birder and active member of the Brookline Bird Club and the Essex County Ornithological Society. Birding is something that not only gets me out of the office but reminds me why I do this work. You can follow my sightings on eBird.

content:
An Annually Updatable Open Ecosystem Mapping Framework Belize holds some of the most biodiverse and ecologically critical landscapes in the Western Hemisphere — spanning submontane pine forests, lowland wetlands, mangrove coastlines, seagrass meadows, and coral reefs. The Belize Ecosystem Atlas is a reproducible, annually updatable scientific framework for mapping and monitoring all of them, from ridge to reef, across more than a decade of environmental change.
11Years Mapped27Ecosystem Types87%Classification AccuracyOpenAccess & Reproducible🗺️ Why This Atlas Needed to Exist Belize has experienced accelerating urbanization, agricultural expansion, and climate-driven environmental change over the past decade. Yet the country’s most recent ecosystem map dated to 2017 — nearly a decade behind the pace of change on the ground. Field-based mapping is too slow and too costly to keep up, leaving policymakers, conservation organizations, and Belizean communities without current data for the decisions that matter most.
The Belize Ecosystem Atlas was built to close that gap. Using satellite remote sensing, Google Earth Engine, and machine learning, we developed a reproducible framework that can be updated annually as new data become available — providing a low-cost, high-accuracy alternative to traditional field inventories. All outputs are openly available for download, giving Belizean agencies, researchers, and conservation organizations direct access to current ecosystem data. This framework is also designed as a transferable template for other tropical countries facing similar mapping gaps.
🌍 Explore the Data Interactively The Belize EcoDynamics Explorer web application is the interactive companion to the Belize Ecosystem Atlas. It lets you explore all 27 ecosystem types across the full 2015–2026 time series directly in your browser — toggle between years, zoom into specific regions, and visualize how Belize’s landscapes have shifted over more than a decade.
🌍 Launch Belize EcoDynamics ExplorerBelize EcoDynamics Explorer runs entirely in your browser via Google Earth Engine — no download or installation required.
🔭 What Is Coming Next The Belize Ecosystem Atlas is a living scientific resource. The next major update will add ecosystem service layers to the existing framework, allowing users to explore not just where ecosystems are, but what they provide to people and communities — from carbon storage and coastal protection to biodiversity support and water regulation.
Planned additions include:
🌿 Carbon Storage & Sequestration 🌊 Coastal Protection & Wave Attenuation 💧 Water Quality Regulation 🐦 Biodiversity & Habitat Quality 🏙️ Nature-Based Solutions Planning Layers If you are a researcher, conservation organization, or government agency interested in collaborating on or contributing to these layers, get in touch!
📥 Access the Data All ecosystem maps are freely available for research, conservation planning, and policy use. To help us track data usage and ensure proper citation, please submit a short data request form.
You will receive download links via email within 48 hours.
📥 Request Data AccessAvailable Data All years are available in the following formats: GeoTIFF (Raster) · Shapefile · KMZ · High Quality PDF · GeoJSON
Year 2026 2025 2024 2023 2022 2021 2020 2019 2018 2017 2016 2015 📝 Suggested Citation
Kelly-Fair, M., Gopal, S., & Koch, M. (in prep). The Belize Ecosystem Atlas: An annually updatable open ecosystem mapping framework for Belize, 2015–2026. Boston University.A Zenodo DOI for this dataset is forthcoming. Check back for an updated citation.⚙️ How It Was Built The Challenge of Ecosystem Mapping at Scale Mapping 27 distinct ecosystem types across an entire country — from coral reefs and seagrass beds to submontane pine forests and mangrove littorals — is not a problem you can solve by hand. The taxonomic depth of the classification, the geographic scale of the study area, and the requirement for annual reproducibility demanded a machine learning approach grounded in the best available remote sensing data.
Variable Selection and Modeling From an initial pool of 290 GIS-derived and remotely sensed variables, we applied a variable importance function within an eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model — implemented in the R caret package — to identify the ten most informative predictors for ecosystem classification:
🏔️ Slope and elevation 👥 Human population count 🌧️ Precipitation 🌊 Bathymetry 🗺️ Two prior Belize ecosystem maps 📡 Sentinel-1 Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) incidence angle 🌡️ Landsat-8 thermal infrared (Band 10) 🌿 Gray-Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) texture measure derived from Landsat-8 Band 5 The full classification was implemented in Google Earth Engine, achieving an overall accuracy of 82.0%, rising to 87.3% after post-classification refinements. The complete codebase is openly available on GitHub so that other researchers and tropical countries facing similar mapping gaps can adapt this framework for their own contexts.
🌿 Ground Truth: Boots on the Ground Numbers and algorithms only go so far. In February 2026, a team from Boston University joined forces with Wild Earth Allies to ground-truth the Atlas classification across Central Belize — hiking into submontane forests, wading through mangroves, and confirming ecosystem boundaries with some of the most experienced botanists and ecologists working in Belize today.
Using a stratified random sampling design, the team confirmed 12 distinct forest types across both lowland and submontane environments, including mangrove, littoral, scrub, moist, pine, and wet forests. The validation data from this expedition directly informed the post-classification adjustments that pushed overall accuracy to 87.3%.

Science belongs to everyone… and so do its benefits.
I am a biogeographer, educator, and data scientist whose work sits at the intersection of remote sensing, ecosystem science, and the communities that depend on these healthy landscapes. Whether you are looking for a dedicated faculty member, a skilled technical collaborator, or a workshop leader who can make complex science accessible, please reach out. I would love to hear from you!
🎓 Academic Appointments My ultimate goal is to join a teaching-forward college or university as a faculty member in geography, environmental science, earth science, or a related field. I am actively on the academic job market and available for positions beginning as early as Fall 2027.
Teaching Philosophy Science belongs to everyone and so do its benefits. My teaching is grounded in the belief that rigorous, accessible science creates better outcomes for communities locally and globally. In the classroom, I emphasize hands-on learning, real-world applications, and the kind of critical thinking that travels with students long after they leave my course.
Courses I Can Teach Introduction to Geographic Information Systems (GIS) Remote Sensing and Earth Observation Meteorology and Climate Change Ecosystem Services and Conservation Biogeography Environmental Data Science Nature-Based Solutions and Climate Adaptation Quantitative Methods in Environmental Science Teaching Experience Graduate Teaching Fellow, Boston University Workshop Instructor in Google Earth Engine, QGIS, and ArcGIS Pro Mentor to undergraduate researchers through the NSF-Strong Coasts program If you are a department chair or hiring committee member I would love to send you my full teaching portfolio and statement. Get in touch!
🛠️ Consulting Services My research expertise translates directly into practical skills for organizations working at the intersection of conservation, data science, and environmental planning. I offer consulting services to NGOs, government agencies, academic institutions, and private organizations. .
What I Offer 🗺️ Custom Ecosystem and Land Cover Mapping Reproducible, satellite-derived ecosystem maps tailored to your study area and conservation planning needs. My work in Belize demonstrates this capability at the national scale across 27 ecosystem types and 11 years of annual data. See the Belize Ecosystem Atlas for more information
📡 Remote Sensing Analysis Multi-sensor satellite data analysis using Landsat, Sentinel-2, Sentinel-1, and other sensots. I can design and execute a full analysis pipeline for change detection, habitat monitoring, and accuracy assessments.
🌍 Google Earth Engine Development Custom GEE scripts, applications, and workflows for large-scale geospatial analysis. I have built production-ready GEE applications including the Belize EcoDynamics Explorer and the forthcoming Belize EcoServices Portal.
💧 Ecosystem Service Assessment Spatial modeling and valuation of ecosystem services including carbon storage, coastal protection, water quality regulation, and biodiversity support. I specialize in working within the Multiscale Integrated Model of Ecosystem Services (MIMES) framework.
📊 Geospatial Data Science End-to-end data science workflows using R, Python, and GIS platforms including ArcGIS and QGIS. From raw data to publication-ready visualizations and reproducible analysis pipelines.
Pricing is project-dependent. Contact me to discuss your needs.
🎤 Workshops I design and deliver workshops that make technical geospatial tools accessible to researchers, practitioners, and students at all levels. Workshops can be delivered in person or remotely and are tailored to your audience and goals.
Current Workshop Offerings Introduction to Google Earth Engine A hands-on introduction to GEE for researchers and practitioners with no prior experience. Covers the code editor, basic remote sensing concepts, and building your first analysis workflow. Suitable for: Beginners, conservation practitioners, graduate students
Remote Sensing for Conservation A practical workshop connecting remote sensing methods to real-world conservation monitoring and planning applications. Suitable for: NGO staff, conservation biologists, land managers
Ecosystem Mapping and Classification A technical workshop covering land cover classification methods, accuracy assessment, and reproducible mapping workflows in GEE and R. Suitable for: Graduate students, researchers, GIS professionals
Introduction to GIS for Environmental Science A beginner-friendly introduction to GIS concepts and tools using QGIS. Suitable for: Undergraduates, early-career researchers, NGO staff
Custom workshops available on request. Let’s talk about what your team needs.
📖 Popular Science Science is for everyone and everyone deserves to understand science. As such, I am currently developing a popular science book exploring ecosystem services — what they are, why they matter, and what we stand to lose as the landscapes that provide them disappear.
If you are a literary agent, editor, or publisher interested in science communication at the intersection of ecology, conservation, and human communities, I would love to connect.
